query: measured latency cost of methods for For the class-matched detections in one capture, select_stage2_subset ranks that DetectionCandidate list with the strategy select_detection already implements. It applies that strategy by the first-maximum rule std::max_element already uses, so a tie keeps the earlier candidate and the later tied candidate stays deferred. It admits at most the count the caller passes, in that rank order, and places every candidate it does not admit into deferred, preserving their order in the candidate list. Each candidate keeps its source_index. Stage2Admission holds those two vectors, admitted and deferred. An empty candidate list returns both vectors empty, and an unknown strategy throws. The pose node calls it with its detection_selection strategy and a count of one, so stage 2 still estimates that single admitted pallet. The admitted source index and the deferred source indices are written on PalletPoseStamped after input_depth_stamp. The message already carries this pair's RGB and depth stamps, so the split is this capture while the scene can still change. When the estimate fails, publish no PalletPoseStamped and write the same two lists on the failure diagnostic, which is the only result that path publishes. The two early returns that publish nothing stay as they are. The user named which detections are sent through stage 2 versus marked deferred. The part they did not name is that the split is these two admission vectors, ordered by that first-maximum rule, on the pose result the handling process reads. on src
findings: The latency that scales is one estimate_pose_chamfer_v3_2 per admitted candidate, not the length of deferred. Liu, Tuzel, Veeraraghavan, and Chellappa (CVPR 2010) measured classic chamfer at 17.59 us per hypothesis and oriented chamfer at 51.50 us, mean over templates of 1,610 points; directional chamfer was 0.40 us and can stop early. Classic chamfer grows linearly with template points. Their directional matcher evaluated 1.05 million hypotheses in 0.42 s, and one object 3D pose took 0.71 s that way against 29.1 s for classic chamfer and 65.3 s for oriented chamfer. The default pocket prototype at contour spacing 0.03 m is 182 points (outer 94, two pockets 44 each). The free search is 31 x 31 x 21 = 20,181 plus 25 x 25 x 13 = 8,125, 28,306 hypotheses. The prior grids run when the free cost is above about 0.00623 m, because prior_lambda 3.0 times (1 - confidence) then exceeds lambda_floor 0.05, and they add 21 x 21 x 21 = 9,261 plus another 8,125, 45,692 hypotheses in all. Scaling 17.59 us by 182/1,610 is about 1.99 us per hypothesis, a serial envelope of about 56 ms for the free grids and about 91 ms if the prior grids also run. That envelope is not a clock of this node: the loop is OpenMP, and it evaluates every cell rather than their early-out directional matcher. The pose node passes a count of one, so that search runs once. Each extra admission repeats it. A deferred candidate does not enter it. An empty candidate list returns both vectors empty and does not call stage 2. An unknown strategy throws before the search. The two early returns that publish nothing add no pose and no DDS hop.

Measured two-stage detectors show the same admission-count multiplier when the second stage is per box. Huang, Rathod, Sun, Zhu, Korattikara, Fathi, Fischer, Wojna, Song, Guadarrama, and Murphy (CVPR 2017, Titan X, batch one) found that Faster R-CNN with Inception-ResNet keeps 96 percent of the accuracy of 300 proposals at 50 proposals and cuts running time by a factor of 3, because the box classifier runs once per proposal. The same cut barely moves R-FCN, because that classifier runs once per image. Zhou, Koltun, and Krahenbuhl (Table 6, ResNet-50, COCO validation, Titan Xp) measured Cascade R-CNN at 66 ms for 1000 proposals, 48 ms for 256, and 42 ms for 64. Ren, He, Girshick, and Sun (Table 4, K40) measured VGG region-wise time, NMS plus pooling plus fully connected layers plus softmax, at 174 ms for about 2000 selective-search proposals and 47 ms for 300 RPN proposals, inside totals of 1830 ms and 198 ms. This node's stage 2 is the per-box kind: chamfer on the admitted crop. A count of one is the small end of that curve. A deferred source index is not another region.

Posing every class-matched detection with a learned refiner has the same per-object multiplier. Labbe, Carpentier, Aubry, and Sivic (CosyPose) measured 190 ms to pose all candidates for 4 views and 6 detections per view, one coarse iteration and one refinement iteration, inside a 320 ms scene (association 40 ms, scene refinement 90 ms). Wen, Yang, Kautz, and Birchfield (FoundationPose) measured 1.3 s per object on an i9-10980XE and RTX 3090 (initialization 4 ms, refinement 0.88 s, selection 0.42 s); tracking is about 32 Hz and is still one object. The distance image inside each chamfer call is the small fixed part of that bill. OpenCV pull 28636, Jetson Orin geometric mean, 640x480 DIST_L2 DIST_MASK_PRECISE on CV_8U is 0.788 ms on 4.x and 0.737 ms with the patch. This node calls cv::distanceTransform with DIST_L2 and DIST_MASK_PRECISE on an 8-bit edge mask once per admitted detection, on the padded face raster rather than a 640x480 frame, so 0.788 ms is that call at the published size. Deferred candidates skip both the grid and that image.

The first-maximum rank and the two admission vectors are not that bill. std::max_element does at most one comparison per element after the first and returns the earliest maximum, which is the tie rule this subset uses. For a count of one that is a single pass over the class-matched list; the deferred vector is the candidates that pass left behind, still in candidate-list order, not a second sort. Kronauer, Pohlmann, Matthe, Smejkal, and Fettweis (ROS 2 Foxy, desktop i7-8700, localhost UDP) measured equal latency at 128 B, 1 KB, and 10 KB; it rose at 100 KB and 500 KB, past the 64 KB UDP fragment. One int32 for the admitted source index and one short int32[] of deferred source indices, written on PalletPoseStamped after input_depth_stamp, sit inside that plateau. The message already carries this pair's RGB and depth stamps. On estimate failure the same two lists ride the diagnostic, the only result that path publishes, and they stay under the 10 KB plateau. The two early returns publish nothing, so they add no DDS hop.
